passage:
9:40 pm.

The mind loop is back: I'm not good enough. Meera got the lead role in the account team. I got a polite "next time." So I lay on the sofa scrolling through everyone's promotion posts until my eyes burned.

Then I made myself stop and take a notebook. Evidence of growth: I cut client complaints on my accounts by half this year. I trained two new joiners. I learned the reporting tool nobody wanted to touch. None of that disappears because I lost one seat.

Saurabh texted, "Dinner Saturday?" I said yes. I won't resign in a rage tonight. Tomorrow I'll ask my manager what the gap was, and give it a few months. If nothing changes, I'll look elsewhere with a clear head.

— Sonali

qa.q: What did Sonali list in the notebook?
qa.a: Sonali listed cutting client complaints on the accounts, training two new joiners and learning a reporting tool nobody else wanted.

qa.q: Why did Sonali stop scrolling, and what was Sonali feeling?
qa.a: Sonali was feeling not good enough and stung by comparison, so Sonali stopped scrolling and wrote evidence of growth to separate the loss from self-worth.

qa.q: What could Sonali do next about staying or leaving?
qa.a: Sonali could ask the manager what the gap was and give it a few months, then decide whether to push here or move on.

qa.q: What might Saurabh be offering with the Saturday invitation?
qa.a: Saurabh may be offering company and a break from rumination, showing that Sonali is valued outside any job title.

grounding: Sonali feels 'I am not good enough' after being passed over, separates performance from worth, lists growth evidence, and plans the next step.
